project_metadata.name: KaraokeZero
project_metadata.repository_strategy: Appliance wrapper deploying and managing upstream PiKaraoke on headless Linux
project_metadata.core_philosophy: Headless execution, direct framebuffer video output via KMS/DRM, analog audio routing, and flash memory wear mitigation.
project_metadata.target_hardware: Raspberry Pi devices with 512 MB to 1 GB RAM (primary optimization target: Raspberry Pi Zero W)

hardware_topology.processing_unit: Raspberry Pi Zero W (Booting OS from MicroSD Card)

storage.sd_card_internal: Dedicated to operating system, Python virtual environments, systemd units, and scripts.
storage.hard_drive_external: USB storage mounted via /etc/fstab to '/mnt/external_hd/karaoke' for media library, SQLite databases, and yt-dlp download buffers.

hardware_topology.video_output: Mini-HDMI to VGA adapter connected to an external monitor or television.

audio_routing.strategy: Analog mixing path with zero software delay and no Pi CPU overhead
audio_routing.extraction: Stereo audio extracted via the 3.5 mm analog output on the active Mini-HDMI to VGA adapter.
audio_routing.mixing: Direct physical line connection from the adapter's 3.5 mm output into an external analog mixer.
audio_routing.microphones: Connected directly to mixer microphone preamps, keeping vocal signals independent of the software stack.

software_stack.operating_system: Raspberry Pi OS Lite (Bookworm 32-bit, headless, systemd)
software_stack.media_player: MPV Media Player (CLI via direct DRM/KMS)
software_stack.video_rendering_engine: Direct Rendering Manager (KMS/DRM) with hardware-accelerated video decoding via mpv (vo=gpu, gpu-context=drm)

admin_panel.purpose: Mobile-first administration portal for song search & background download, PiKaraoke system settings, hardware diagnostics, power controls, and headless Wi-Fi onboarding.
logic_flow: 1. Serves a 3-tab mobile web app: Songs (search & yt-dlp downloads), System (PiKaraoke settings & power controls), and Wi-Fi.
2. NetworkManager is configured to favor an administrator fallback hotspot (Priority 100).
3. User connects to the configuration portal via smartphone browser at http://<ip>:8888.
4. Performs background serialized downloads of karaoke videos with quality throttling and best audio bitrate.
5. Toggles PiKaraoke guest access (online YouTube search vs local-only) and synchronizes config.ini.
6. Provisions venue Wi-Fi credentials with Priority 50 and handles system reboot/shutdown.

orchestrator.purpose: Background daemon coordinating PiKaraoke queue states with direct-to-framebuffer video playback.
logic_flow: 1. Validate external storage binding on boot: if configured external storage is absent, disconnected, or unreadable, display a dedicated graphical warning screen via MPV DRM/KMS and halt boot in zero-write safe mode until reconnected or rebooted.
2. Identify active IP address on the primary wireless interface and generate connection QR code via qrencode.
3. Poll PiKaraoke REST API (/api/queue) for upcoming songs and track status.
4. IDLE STATE: Launch graphical idle details screen (or optional background video) via mpv direct DRM/KMS, displaying IP and dynamic connection QR code.
5. PLAYING STATE: Stop idle screen and spawn mpv targeting the active song stream using DRM/KMS GPU acceleration (vo=gpu, gpu-context=drm).
6. TRACK COMPLETION: Terminate mpv, notify PiKaraoke backend, release GPU resources, and return to idle state.

desktop_downloader.purpose: Lightweight, zero-pip desktop utility allowing users to batch download high-volume karaoke tracks from YouTube directly on their Linux PC at full speed.
desktop_downloader.tech_stack: Python 3 (standard library http.server), yt-dlp, ffmpeg, HTML5, Vanilla CSS, Vanilla JS
logic_flow: 1. Launched via ready-to-run root executable `./karaoke-downloader` with automated dependency diagnostics (Python 3, ffmpeg, yt-dlp).
2. Automatically launches user's default browser targeting local web UI on port 7777 (or next available port).
3. Auto-detects connected USB drives and external KaraokeZero drives (/media/$USER/*, /mnt/*) to save directly to the songs folder.
4. YouTube search engine parses rich metadata, channel names, durations, and high-res video thumbnails in ~250ms with zero Google API keys.
5. Supports single song search, YouTube playlist inspection & selective download, and batch plain-text song list imports.

6. Strictly enforces H.264 (AVC1) video and AAC/M4A audio in MP4 container (`--merge-output-format mp4`, `-S vcodec:h264,res,acodec:m4a`) to guarantee 100% hardware-accelerated playback on Raspberry Pi Zero W.
7. Maintains a local download archive (`download_archive.txt`) on the target drive to skip duplicates seamlessly.

installer.purpose: Automated host provisioning script for Raspberry Pi OS Lite.
actions: Install system packages: mpv, python3-flask, network-manager, qrencode, yt-dlp, python3-pil.
Configure /etc/fstab and /etc/karaokezero/storage.env for external USB drive mount persistence.
Fetch latest upstream PiKaraoke release and configure Python virtual environments under PEP 668.
Install, enable, and verify systemd service units (admin_panel, orchestrator, pikaraoke).

performance_and_stability_guarantees.ram_management: mpv processes are recycled between songs to reclaim memory and GPU framebuffers; no web browser runs on the host.
performance_and_stability_guarantees.cpu_management: Video decoding offloaded via DRM/KMS hardware acceleration; microphone audio is mixed in the analog domain.
performance_and_stability_guarantees.sd_card_protection: Zero-Write Rootfs architecture with volatile in-memory journald logging, disk logging daemons permanently masked (rsyslog, logrotate), /var/log mounted as in-memory tmpfs, automatic OS updates disabled and masked (apt-daily, unattended-upgrades), disabled flash swap paging, rootfs mounted with noatime,commit=60,errors=remount-ro, and automated non-interactive fsck kernel recovery on dirty power cuts (fsck.repair=yes). All write-intensive processes (SQLite database in WAL mode, yt-dlp buffers, media downloads, and venue Wi-Fi credentials) are routed to external USB storage. At runtime, venue Wi-Fi credentials operate from transient RAM (/run), keeping the MicroSD card free of venue writes and preserving credentials across re-installations. If external drive is absent or unreadable, boot is frozen on an alert screen to guarantee zero fallback writes or phantom files on the MicroSD card.
